Isotopic labelling The symbol for the isotope introduced is placed in square brackets directly attached to the part of the name to which it refers (e.g. sodium ('4C]formate); appropriate arabic numerals and prefixes are added as necessary (e.g. L-[2-C]leucine). For simple molecules, chemical formulae may be used (e.g. 4#CO,). Square brackets should not be used when the isotopic symbol is attached to a word that is not a chemical name (e.g. “!*C-labelled”). Terms such as “'![-labelled albumin” should not be contracted to [3!T]albumin since native albumin does not contain iodine.

Genetics Genes and chromosomes The International Committee on Standardizing Human Gene No-menclature has developed a system knownas the International System. for Human Gene Nomenclature, but this is not universally accepted. Human genes are generally denoted by italicized symbols composed of capital letters, sometimes with the addition of an arabic numeral (e.g. CF, G6PD).
